## Proof

Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the three real roots of $x^3-6x-2=0$. By Vieta's formulas:
$$\alpha+\beta+\gamma=0,\qquad \alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha=-6,\qquad \alpha\beta\gamma=2.$$

Each root satisfies $x^3=6x+2$, so
$$\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3=6(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)+6=6,$$
$$\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^2-2(\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha)=0-2(-6)=12,$$
$$\alpha^4+\beta^4+\gamma^4=6(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2)+2(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)=72.$$

### The two quadratics come from the two cyclic orderings

The three calibration points are $(\alpha,\beta),(\beta,\gamma),(\gamma,\alpha)$. A cyclic relabeling $\alpha\to\beta\to\gamma\to\alpha$ sends this set to itself, so it produces the same quadratic. The $6$ permutations of the roots split into $2$ cyclic classes (the two cosets of $A_3$ in $S_3$), giving exactly **two** distinct quadratics — matching the problem statement.

### Setting up equations for $Q(x)=ax^2+bx+c$

**Sum of values.** $Q(\alpha)+Q(\beta)+Q(\gamma)=\beta+\gamma+\alpha=0$, so
$$a(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2)+b(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)+3c=12a+3c=0 \implies c=-4a.$$

**Weighted by roots.** $\alpha Q(\alpha)+\beta Q(\beta)+\gamma Q(\gamma)=\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha=-6$, so
$$a(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3)+b(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2)+c(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)=6a+12b=-6 \implies a+2b=-1.$$

**Weighted by squares.** $\alpha^2 Q(\alpha)+\beta^2 Q(\beta)+\gamma^2 Q(\gamma)=\alpha^2\beta+\beta^2\gamma+\gamma^2\alpha=:S$, so
$$a(\alpha^4+\beta^4+\gamma^4)+b(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3)+c(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2)=72a+6b+12c=24a+6b=S.$$

### Evaluating $S$ and $S'$

Let $S=\alpha^2\beta+\beta^2\gamma+\gamma^2\alpha$ and $S'=\alpha^2\gamma+\gamma^2\beta+\beta^2\alpha$ (the other cyclic order). Then
$$S+S'=\alpha^2(\beta+\gamma)+\beta^2(\gamma+\alpha)+\gamma^2(\alpha+\beta)=-(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3)=-6,$$
$$S-S'=\alpha^2(\beta-\gamma)+\beta^2(\gamma-\alpha)+\gamma^2(\alpha-\beta)=-(\alpha-\beta)(\beta-\gamma)(\gamma-\alpha).$$

The discriminant of $x^3-6x-2$ is $-4(-6)^3-27(-2)^2=864-108=756=(\alpha-\beta)^2(\beta-\gamma)^2(\gamma-\alpha)^2$, so
$$(\alpha-\beta)(\beta-\gamma)(\gamma-\alpha)=\pm 6\sqrt{21}.$$

Hence $S-S'=\mp 6\sqrt{21}$, giving the two values
$$S=-3-3\sqrt{21}\quad\text{or}\quad S=-3+3\sqrt{21}.$$

### Solving for $a,b,c$

From $24a+6b=S$ and $a+2b=-1$ (so $b=(-1-a)/2$):
$$24a+3(-1-a)=S \implies 21a-3=S \implies a=\frac{S+3}{21}.$$

**Case 1:** $S=-3-3\sqrt{21}$, so $a=-\dfrac{\sqrt{21}}{7}$, $\;c=\dfrac{4\sqrt{21}}{7}$, $\;b=\dfrac{-7+\sqrt{21}}{14}$.
$$Q(1)=a+b+c=\frac{-2\sqrt{21}+(-7+\sqrt{21})+8\sqrt{21}}{14}=\frac{7\sqrt{21}-7}{14}=\frac{\sqrt{21}-1}{2}.$$

**Case 2:** $S=-3+3\sqrt{21}$, so $a=\dfrac{\sqrt{21}}{7}$, $\;c=-\dfrac{4\sqrt{21}}{7}$, $\;b=\dfrac{-7-\sqrt{21}}{14}$.
$$Q(1)=a+b+c=\frac{2\sqrt{21}+(-7-\sqrt{21})-8\sqrt{21}}{14}=\frac{-7\sqrt{21}-7}{14}=-\frac{\sqrt{21}+1}{2}.$$

### Numerical sanity check

With approximate roots $\alpha\approx2.601,\;\beta\approx-0.340,\;\gamma\approx-2.261$: interpolating through $(\alpha,\beta),(\beta,\gamma),(\gamma,\alpha)$ gives $a\approx0.655=\sqrt{21}/7$ (Case 2) and $Q(1)\approx-2.791=-(\sqrt{21}+1)/2$. The reverse cyclic order gives $Q(1)\approx1.791=(\sqrt{21}-1)/2$. Both confirmed.

### Conclusion

The two values of $Q(1)$ are $\dfrac{\sqrt{21}-1}{2}$ and $-\dfrac{\sqrt{21}+1}{2}$. Since $\sqrt{21}\approx4.58$,
$$\frac{\sqrt{21}-1}{2}\approx 1.79 \;>\; -\frac{\sqrt{21}+1}{2}\approx -2.79.$$

$$\boxed{\dfrac{\sqrt{21}-1}{2}}$$
